title: Community Conversations: Local Impacts of Medicaid and SNAP Cuts
description:
The Big Ugly Bill has passed the house and now is the time to make your voice heard. The bill calls for devastating cuts to Medicaid, SNAP, and the safety net, all to pay for tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy. Pennsylvania voters, like voters in other states, strongly support these programs, and with good reason. Medicaid provides critical support for millions of Pennsylvanians.

The reconciliation bill will terminate healthcare coverage for around 13 million Americans and kick approximately 3 million Americans off of SNAP. While new requirements for the state to help pay for the SNAP program would result in new expenditures for the state of $226 million to over a billion. The bill does all this harm while adding $2.4 trillion to the federal deficit.

This event is open to everyone. Join Pennsylvanians Together and the Pennsylvania Policy Center, for a real conversation about proposals that could harm Pennsylvanians, and what we can do about them. We will have experts to discuss what these cuts mean for us and our communities as well as explain what you can do to fight the cuts.

description:

title: No Kings/Kick Out the Clowns
description:
On June 14, our clown-king will honor himself with a four-mile military parade in our nation’s capitol. This tacky parade will cost taxpayers millions of dollars. Join us in protest of this ridiculous example of government waste.

WHEN: Saturday, June 14 from 5 - 8 PM

WHERE: TX Capitol Front Steps

BRING: EVERYONE. Bring your family and friends and your creative protest signs (No sticks longer than 12 inches are allowed by Capitol DPS including flag poles.)

Our grassroots street circus will turn satire into resistance and reclaim the big tent for democracy.

Women’s March KICK OUT THE CLOWNS: When you elect clowns, the country becomes a circus. 🤡 This will be a day of bold, creative actions in protest of the chaos that has been sown across the country. Together, we’ll set a national record for the most circuses held in a single day while we simultaneously refuse to celebrate a petty clown who desperately wants to be seen as strong. We won’t stop until we build the country we all deserve.

Indivisible’s NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption. The flag doesn’t belong to those that seek to destroy our country - it belongs to us. Join us to make history.

MOBILITY: We will be marching around the TX Capitol, not outside of Capitol grounds. If you have mobility concerns, you are welcome to stand firm at the front steps of the TX Capitol. Capitol bathrooms are ADA accessible.

DEETS: Bathrooms are available inside the Capitol. You will have to pass through a DPS security checkpoint to access bathrooms. Emergency water will be available on-site but please bring your own.

TRANSPORTATION & PARKING: CAPMETRO bus lines 1, 10, 103, 20, and 3 drop off near the Capitol, plan your trip. Please park at the Capitol Visitors Parking Garage (free for the first 2 hours), or park on the street in the neighborhoods west of the TX Capitol using the Park ATX app with discount codes: FREE15ATX1, FREE15ATX2

KEEP IN MIND: Soliciting donations and selling products is not allowed on Capitol grounds. We respect the DPS rules so that we can continue to have impactful mass mobilization efforts on OUR Capitol grounds!

SAFETY: We have a team of volunteers, legal observers, and street medics coming to this event. If you would like to volunteer for any of these teams, please use this form to contact us!

Veteran? We have a veterans arm of Hands Off Central TX. Plug in on-site to defend democracy, the constitution, and our first amendment rights. Email your interest to veterans@handsoffcentraltx.org

Nonviolent Protest Disclaimer: Nobody from our organization will be provocative and we are not planning civil disobedience. We are utilizing our First Amendment right to protest and our right to lobby our representative government. We do everything in our power to protect the civil rights and physical safety of everyone at our events. We have yet to have any significant incidents of safety issues at any of our events.

By attending our events, you are implicitly agreeing that while you attend our event, you will respect the laws and constitution of the United States and State of Texas and not create or contribute to a safety issue or lawlessness for our attendees and neighbors. We protect our community and defend democracy - we do not put people at risk or threaten violence.

title: Sunrise New Orleans Panel Toxic Legacies: Environmental Racism and Resistance in Louisiana
description:
CALLING ALL ALLIES AND BIPOC COMMUNITY MEMBERS!

Show up or tune in for Toxic Legacies: Environmental Racism and Resistance in Louisiana, a panel this Friday, June 13, from 6 pm to 8 pm CST (4 pm to 6 pm PT, 7 pm to 9 pm EST) at Cafe Istanbul (2372 St. Claude Avenue)

The Trump administration is greenlighting the expansion of the fossil fuel industry in Louisiana, impacting historic black and indigenous communities and fueling the climate crisis. This is happening while coastal communities in Louisiana face dangerous cuts to local disaster preparation funding, opening the door to harm in our most vulnerable communities, and adding to the ongoing record of environmental racism in Louisiana.

Louisianians are experiencing hotter summers, increased marsh fires, more frequent saltwater intrusion in the Mississippi River, and increased vulnerability to storms due to the ongoing climate crisis. The Trump Administration and Billionaires are fueling the flames, and we need solidarity now more than ever to grasp the intersections and causes of our oppression, and explore how the liberation of nationally oppressed peoples is impossible without climate justice.

As part of the Black, Latine, and Indigenous Sunrise Movement 2025 Caucus Gathering in New Orleans this week, the Sunrise New Orleans hub is hosting a panel presentation on the historic and ongoing context of environmental racism in Louisiana. The hub is bringing together local BIPOC climate justice organizers to speak on the issues we are facing and how we are organizing to fight back against Trump and the Billionaires attacking the climate justice movement, and fueling the climate crisis. 

Featuring speakers from Rise St. James, Greater New Orleans Interfaith Climate Coalition, Union Migrante, and Sunrise Movement New Orleans.

Other participating and supporting organizations include the Louisiana Bucket Brigade, Healthy Gulf, Stop the Grain Train, Climate Reality Project, Party for Socialism and Liberation, New Orleans DSA, and Freedom Road Socialist Organization, and more.

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

title: End ICE Collusion in California — Tell AG Rob Bonta: Investigate & Act Now
description:
California has positioned itself as a sanctuary state — but many local jails and law enforcement agencies are still working with ICE in ways that undermine this promise.

These quiet arrangements — including transfers, detention contracts, and data sharing — often take place outside public view, disproportionately harming Black, brown, and immigrant communities.

This action invites you to join a growing call for **California Attorney General Rob Bonta** to:

- Conduct a full investigation into ICE-related practices across the state  
- Release a public report identifying jurisdictions involved  
- Use the power of his office to bring local practice in line with state sanctuary law

We’re asking Californians to take a clear but principled stand.

**✍🏾 Add your name now to urge the Attorney General to act — and help ensure our communities are protected from further harm.**
